decisionsTitle: Volunteer roles in configurable categories, each with a contact person
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-14, the night after the volunteers' own page shipped (§768):** «Pentru „ce sunt dispus să fac” trebuie să am categorii cu sub-categorii, eg: aș pune activități Start/Finish și am putea adăuga ex: direcționare, foto/video, punct hidratare; Traseu: direcționare, punct hidratare, foto/video. Toate astea configurabile.» And, twice: «trebuie să fie o persoană de contact pentru voluntari» — «the contact person for each category will be established later». And «it's YOLO man»: the open points were decided here and are said below. Amends §761 (the roles a person ticks), §764 (the badge's role and telephone), §765 (the role's form and description), §768 (the volunteers' page, the guardian's request) and §751 / §754 (the event's file). Builds on the stacked work of the same night (the counts tick, the date of birth).

**A. The model.** A new table `event_volunteer_categories` (the event, the name in both languages, `sort`, a **contact person** — name, telephone, email, every one nullable, empty when the category is made — and the stamps) and a nullable `event_volunteer_roles.category_id` (migration `0160`, expand-only). **«Alte activități» / “Other activities”** is the heading of the roles under no category — every role from before the categories, and any the club leaves unfiled; no row stands for it, so it can be neither renamed nor deleted, and it is drawn only when the event has a category at all (an event with none lists its roles as it always did, with no heading). At most twelve categories to an event; a name once per event, in each language, whatever the case. **The same role name may stand in several categories and not twice in one**: the unique indexes are on the event, the category (the nil uuid stands for «none», so the unfiled roles are one group of their own), and `lower(name)` in each language, with the service saying so first (`VOLUNTEER_NAME_TAKEN`, naming the box). Nothing enforced a role's name before, so the migration **numbers a name typed twice on one event** — the first keeps it, the later ones become «Punct de apă (2)», and a number that itself collides with a name already there («A», «a» and «A (2)») is told apart once more by the start of the row's id — before the index, so it can never refuse to run against a database that already has such a pair. `category_id` is `NO ACTION`, not `RESTRICT`: deleting an **event** cascades to the categories and the roles in no promised order, and the immediate check of `RESTRICT` would refuse the whole delete when the categories went first; the end-of-statement check sees both gone (the choices' own lesson, §761), while a category with a role under it is still refused — by the service with its own sentence (`VOLUNTEER_CATEGORY_HAS_ROLES`) and, behind it, by the database.

**B. The «Voluntari» card.** A fold **«Categorii»** — «Adaugă o categorie» (both names, «Copiază și tradu tot» filling the English one — the house's one button, scoped to the form, which already knew `nameEn`), a row per category with its two names, «Roluri: n» (how many roles sit under it) and, in words, its contact; ↑ / ↓ (the roles' own pattern, the arrows drawn only where a step is possible); «Modifică» (the names, and «Șterge categoria», which asks first and is refused with a sentence while any role is under it); and **«Persoana de contact»** — three optional boxes with a «Salvează» of their own, audited `volunteer_category.contact_edited` with **the boxes that changed and never their words** (a contact is a third person's name and number; the trail of every other edit names fields, never values). The telephone is read by the parser every staff phone box uses (`typedPhone`), bounded, and **must be written like a telephone number** (`isPhoneNumberShaped`, the check «Telefon public» and the badge share — never rejected for being foreign or a landline, refused as words, naming its box); the address must be one. Each verb asserts the role on the server (`canManageVolunteers`: the Organizer and the Administrators; the Tehnic role, the Redactor, a volunteer and a member are refused whatever the card drew, BR-REQ-060-01), under the event's lock and the categories' in id order — the order a role's change takes them. **«Categoria»** is a native select on «Adaugă un rol» and each role's «Modifică» (the house's choice control, as «Rolul dat»; never a toggle), «Alte activități» first; it is drawn only once the event has a category, and a form that posts none leaves the role where it is. The card lists the roles under their category's heading in the category's order; ↑ / ↓ on a role move it **inside its category** (the others' places untouched); a role moved to another category goes to the end of it. **Decided:** a role is **named alone as «Direcționare (Traseu)»** wherever it is read apart from its heading — the «Dă-i rolul …» buttons and select, the chips, the person's tick list and select, the volunteers' own groups, the email's «Rol: …» and «Dă-i rolul», the CSV's two role columns, the organizers' notice line, the staff person page (the art. 15 view), the agreement's `{{volunteerRole}}` / `{{volunteerRoleChoices}}` / `{{volunteerChoiceTasks}}` sentences and the card's comparison with what an accepted agreement named (so a role moved to another category says the accepted text named other roles, as a renamed one always did) — and **the badge's band shows the role only** (the owner's brief said «decide: default the band shows the role only»); «Câte ecusoane» lists the roles under their categories, each pile titled with its category.

**C. The volunteers' page.** The roles are drawn under a **level-3 heading per category**, in the category's order, each with its tick, description and count line exactly as before (the stacked tick still decides whether a number is said); a category with no role still needing people is not drawn, the roles under none follow under «Alte activități», and an event with no category — or a page cached before categories existed — draws no heading at all. Under a category's heading, **when its contact is set, one line**: «Întrebări? <nume> · <telefon> · <email>», the telephone a `tel:` link (the stored digits) read grouped («+40 712 345 678», `formatPhone`, here and in the card's line, the emails and the badge) and the address a `mailto:` one. **Decided, on the tap targets:** the first link takes `INLINE_TAP_TARGET` (44 pixels that do not stretch the line), a later one `TAP_TARGET`'s own shape — the contact page's rule (§480): the first link's reach above its words would otherwise cover the lower half of a line the second wrapped under it. The event page's callout names a role once though it may stand in two categories.

**D. The contact in the volunteers' emails.** «Ți-am primit oferta», «Rolul tău» and the parent's request carry, in their footer — beside the reply line, in both halves of the bilingual message — «Întrebări despre voluntariat? <nume> · <telefon> · <email>» / “Questions about volunteering? …” — with no full stop after the address (a stop there reads as part of it; the reply line, when it follows, is joined by one): the contact of the category of **the role given** when there is one, else of **the roles the person offered for** — each person once, joined by «; » and, when there are two or more, each with its category («Traseu: Ana · …; Start / Sosire: Dan · …»), and none for a role under no category or a category with no contact. Not in the organizers' notice, the agreement's two messages or any copy to the club; plain words, no link, so a mail client makes of them what it does. **Never in the CSV**, whose role cells say «Direcționare (Traseu)» and nothing of the contact. **On the badges:** «Telefonul coordonatorului» ticked **with no number typed** — which the designer refused before — now prints, on each role's badge, the telephone of the contact person of the role's category with the design's label; a number typed in the designer wins on every role; a role under no category, or a category with no telephone, prints no telephone line, but **the row stays on every badge while the tick is on** (blank there), so the badges of a sheet are cut alike and the designer's crop box is true for each. The saved design is unchanged by it (the number stays empty); the stamp of the picture includes the category's telephone, so a new contact is a new picture.

**E. The event's JSON file (§751) — decided, and flagged.** The brief asked the file to carry the categories and «each role's category», which cannot be said without the roles: the file carried none (§754: the roles «belong to one date», a copy starts with none). **Decided:** the file gains a key of its own beside the event, `volunteers` — the categories in the club's order with their contact, the roles with both names, how many each needs, the description's document, the colour and their category **by its place in the list** (never an id), and never a person, a choice, an acceptance or the tick «Primește voluntari». A file made before has none and reads as an event with nothing to bring. «Ca eveniment nou» writes them into the new draft **through the card's own services** (so every rule of the card holds and each write is audited), reading the file forgivingly — a place that points at no category is «Alte activități», a contact the card would refuse (an address that is none) is left out, a colour no word reads on costs the colour and not the role, an entry the card itself refuses (a name twice under one category) is skipped and the rest of the event is not held up; the audit counts how many were written and how many left out, never what, and the result says it in a note («volunteersSkipped»). **An import over an existing event leaves its roles and categories as they are** — a role may have people on it — and the diff, which compares the event's own configuration, shows none of it — the preview says so in words, as it says a series' rule is not applied. The contact is the club's published business contact, so it is in a file the club hands to itself; the version stays 3 (an optional key with a default, the badges' own precedent). If the owner would rather the file stay as §754 said, `readVolunteersFile` and `importVolunteersFile` are the two calls to remove.

**F. Privacy.** The contact is the club's organizer's business contact, **published by the club's own choice** on a public page and in the club's own messages — nothing of a participant's or a volunteer's, no new purpose, no new retention — so **the privacy notice's template needs no change** and no text is approved again for it. The card's help says to name only a person who agreed to be on a public page, and behind its «?» that the telephone also goes on the badges of the category's roles when the design has no number of its own and that the contact is in the event's file, not the CSV. The category's words and contact live as long as the event; the sample race's two categories are seed content for local and QA only, never production (§30).

**G. Sample content.** `yarn db:seed` gives the sample race two categories — «Start / Sosire» and «Traseu» — with the owner's example roles under each (Direcționare, Foto/Video, Punct de hidratare), no contact set; the seed refuses production.

**A paper agreement already printed** is stamped by the roles' ids, as before: renaming or moving a role or a category after printing is not refused at «Semnat pe hârtie», and the record names the new words — so SETUP §44 says to print again after such a change (as it says that categorising a role people already signed for adds a note on their rows and leaves the signatures valid); putting the printed words into the stamp was left out, it would change a contract three services and their tests share, for a gap that began with role renames.

**Refused.** A role held in two categories at once (a role is one row with one category); sub-categories of categories (the owner's «sub-categorii» are the roles under a heading: two levels, the second being the roles themselves); a fixed list of categories (they are the club's words, per event); showing the category on the badge's band; a contact person in the CSV; the contact in the organizers' notice (the colleagues have the card); a category's heading at all on an event with none; a unique constraint that could refuse the migration on data already there; `RESTRICT` on the role's category (it refuses an event's own delete); applying the file's volunteers over an existing event.
changelogLine: - **Volunteer roles in categories, each with a contact person** — the «Voluntari» card gets a «Categorii» fold (add, rename, reorder, delete while empty, each with an optional «Persoana de contact») and every role a «Categoria»; the volunteers' page groups the roles under their category's heading with the contact on one line; the contact is in the volunteers' emails' footer and, on a badge with no number typed, the coordinator's telephone; the same role name may stand in several categories, told apart as «Direcționare (Traseu)»; the event's JSON file carries the categories and roles (the import says what it leaves out). Migration `0160`. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends the volunteers' card criteria (§761, §765, §768). Given the event's «Voluntari» card, then a fold «Categorii» adds a category with its name in both languages (both or neither, at most twelve, a name once per event whatever the case), renames it, moves it one step up or down, saves its optional «Persoana de contact» — a name, a telephone number and an email, each optional and empty when the category is made — the telephone written like a telephone number, words refused naming its box — with a «Salvează» of its own — and deletes it only while no role sits under it, refused with a sentence otherwise; each role's «Categoria» is a choice among the categories and «Alte activități», a form that draws no such choice leaves the role where it is, a role moved to another category goes to the end of it and ↑ / ↓ on a role move it inside its own category; every verb is refused for a role that may not manage volunteers whatever the card drew, and the audit trail names the boxes that changed and never a contact's words (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the same role name under two categories of one event, then both stand — the person's choices, the role given, the «De repartizat» chips, the select, the CSV's role columns, the email's role and the agreement's sentences name each as «Direcționare (Traseu)» in the reader's language — and the same name twice under one category, or twice among the roles under none, is refused in either language whatever the case (`VOLUNTEER_NAME_TAKEN` and the database's unique indexes); the badge's band prints the role only; a category with a role under it cannot be deleted by the service or the database, while deleting the event takes the categories and the roles together (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Migration `0160_volunteer_role_categories` is expand-only: it adds `event_volunteer_categories` and the nullable `event_volunteer_roles.category_id`, and unique indexes on the role's name per event, category and language; every role from before keeps no category, a role name typed twice on one event is numbered before the index — a number that collides with a name already there told apart once more — so the migration cannot refuse it, and a person's role, choices and state are untouched (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends the volunteers' page criteria (§761, §768). Given an event whose roles sit under categories, when a visitor opens `/ro/evenimente/<slug>/voluntari`, then the roles are listed under a level-3 heading per category in the club's order, each with its tick, description and count line as before; a category with no role still needing people is not shown, the roles under none follow under «Alte activități», and an event with no category shows no heading at all; and under the heading of a category whose contact is set there is one line «Întrebări? <name> · <phone> · <email>» with the telephone as a `tel:` link and the address as a `mailto:` one, each at least 44 pixels tall, and no line for a category with none (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a volunteer's «am primit», the message naming the role the organizers gave them, or the request to their parent or guardian, when the category of the role given — else of the roles offered for — has a contact person, then the footer of both halves of the message says «Întrebări despre voluntariat? <name> · <phone> · <email>» / “Questions about volunteering? …” with the telephone grouped and no full stop after the address, each contact once — each with its category when there are two or more — and none for a role under no category; the organizers' notice, the agreement's messages and a copy to the club carry none, and the CSV never holds a contact (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a volunteer badge's design with «Telefonul coordonatorului» ticked and no number typed, then it is saved, and each role's badge prints the telephone of the contact person of the role's category with the design's label — a role under no category or a category with no telephone prints none, the row staying blank on its badge so every badge is cut alike — while a number typed in the design is printed on every role; the sheet and the picture say the same line; «Câte ecusoane» lists the roles under their categories (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event's JSON file (§751), then it carries the volunteers' categories with their contact and the roles with their category by its place in the list — never a person, a choice, an acceptance, an id or the tick «Primește voluntari»; «Ca eveniment nou» writes them to the new draft through the card's own rules, reading the file forgivingly (an unknown category is «Alte activități», a contact the card would refuse is left out, an entry the card refuses is skipped), a file made before reads as nothing to bring, an import as a new event says how many entries it left out, and an import over an existing event leaves its roles and categories as they are and says so (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: volunteer roles in configurable categories, each with a contact person
